subject: botany_2
question_text: Write the physiological responses of gibberellins in plants.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.26, printed question 21. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK NOTE: the guide's first line lists "Leaf and fruit senescence" among the effects of gibberellins and its own point 7 then says "They delay senescence." NCERT is clear that gibberellins DELAY senescence; the card writes the delay and records the contradiction. The guide also prints "fruit repining" for ripening. Revised 2026-09-05: the s2_stem WHY and memory tip no longer say every listed response is internode elongation, because the apple response is fruit growth.

insider_note: The named numbers are what lift this answer: GA3 in brewing, and 20 tonnes an acre in sugarcane. Write at least one of them.

steps.label: What gibberellins are
steps.margin_note: Name the family and the numbering. Four lines.
lines: Gibberellins are plant growth hormones.
There are more than a hundred of them, written
GA1, GA2, GA3 and so on.
GA3 was the first one discovered and is the
most studied.
steps.why: Gibberellins are a numbered family rather than one molecule, which is why answers name a particular one, GA3, when a use is specific.
common_mistakes: Writing gibberellin as a single compound. It is a large family, numbered GA1, GA2, GA3.
Confusing GA3 with 2,4-D. 2,4-D is a synthetic AUXIN.
steps.memory_tip: A numbered family, and GA3 is the one that does the named jobs.

steps.label: Stem and fruit responses
steps.margin_note: Four numbered responses. Bolting is worth naming explicitly.
lines: 1. Gibberellins cause elongation of the stem
axis. They increase the length of grape stalks.
2. They cause fruits such as apple to elongate
and improve their shape.
3. They restore normal height in genetically
DWARF and ROSETTE plants.
4. They cause BOLTING, the elongation of
internodes just before flowering.
steps.why: Stem-axis elongation is the action behind most of these: it is why grape stalks lengthen, why a dwarf plant reaches normal height and why a rosette plant bolts. The apple response is the same growth-promoting effect acting on the fruit rather than the stem.
common_mistakes: Saying gibberellins shorten the stem. They ELONGATE it.
Leaving out bolting. It is the named response and appears as a question on its own.
steps.memory_tip: Gibberellin promotes elongation: of the stem axis, of grape stalks and of the apple fruit.

steps.label: Industrial and crop uses
steps.margin_note: Three named uses with the numbers. The numbers are the mark.
lines: 5. GA3 speeds up the MALTING process in the
brewing industry.
6. Spraying GA on sugarcane stems increases
stem length and raises the yield by about
20 tonnes per acre.
7. GA hastens the maturity period of conifers,
so seed is produced earlier.
steps.why: Sugarcane stores its sugar in the stem, so anything that lengthens the stem directly raises the sugar harvested.
common_mistakes: Giving no figures. The 20 tonnes per acre is what makes this a real answer.
Saying GA slows maturity in conifers. It HASTENS it.
steps.memory_tip: Longer sugarcane stem means more stored sugar.

steps.label: Senescence and maturity
steps.margin_note: State the delay clearly. The guide prints both answers, so be unambiguous.
lines: 8. Gibberellins DELAY senescence, so fruits can
be left on the tree longer and still be
transported.
9. They break seed and bud dormancy.
10. They induce flowering in long day plants.
steps.why: Delaying senescence keeps the tissue alive and working longer, which is the opposite of what ethylene and abscisic acid do.
common_mistakes: Writing that gibberellins promote senescence. They DELAY it. The guide's own list contradicts itself on this line.
Confusing this with ethylene, which PROMOTES senescence and abscission.
steps.memory_tip: Gibberellin delays the end; ethylene brings it on.
